title: What If All of Antarctica's Ice Melted?

scenes.text: What if all of Antarctica's ice melted? Every coastline on Earth would be redrawn.
Antarctica holds enough ice to raise the sea about 60 meters. That's roughly 200 feet.
Low-lying coastal cities would be flooded, and the map of the continents would change.
Melting just West Antarctica alone would still raise sea level by about six meters.
Right now it's losing well over a hundred billion tons of ice a year, and that is speeding up.
Today Greenland and Antarctica together add only about 1.2 millimeters a year. The giant is just waking up.

description:
What if all of Antarctica's ice melted?
It holds enough ice to raise global sea level by about 60 meters, and NASA data show it is already losing mass.
What should we run through next?
